mechanism_narrative: The monotonic four-week rise in TRANSIT mobility from -35.0 to -20.1 percent below baseline signals restored commuting and leisure travel; this travel recovery will continue to lift RETAIL_REC, making the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC higher than the last 28-day mean.
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite TRANSIT rising in each of the last four weekly readings.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM crosses above +15 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weeks, household provisioning normalizes and discretionary shopping resumes, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds +15 percent change from baseline for two consecutive weekly readings
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls or stays flat over the next 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM has exceeded +15 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The joint movement of falling RESIDENTIAL mobility and rising TRANSIT mobility indicates a behavioral shift from staying home to out-of-home activity; this interaction amplifies retail trips, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next 28 days.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below +15 and TRANSIT rises above -25 in the same week
failure_condition: When RESIDENTIAL is below +15 and TRANSIT is above -25, the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: In a reopening regime where TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both less negative than their four-week averages, office return policies drive weekday retail footfall; RETAIL_REC will rise over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: In weeks classified as reopening, RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than over the prior 28 days when WORKPLACES improves.

mechanism_narrative: The steady decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility from +19.1 to +13.7 percent above baseline shows people spending less time at home; this behavioral release will directly increase RETAIL_REC over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC in the next 7 days is lower than or equal to its level in the last 7 days while RESIDENTIAL continues to decline.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility rebounding above -23 percent change from baseline signals a policy-driven return to offices, which increases weekday retail traffic; RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises above -23 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: After WORKPLACES rises above -23, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the preceding 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal improvement in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM mobility during the spring transition increases outdoor and essential trips, which spill over into retail-and-recreation; RETAIL_REC will rise over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: The next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than the last 14-day mean while PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improve.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT improvement accelerates and RETAIL_REC remains above -30, the interaction between transit recovery and retail momentum produces further retail gains; RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week increase exceeds 3 points and RETAIL_REC is above -30
failure_condition: After a week with TRANSIT gain over 3 points and RETAIL_REC above -30, the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than the current 7-day mean.
